newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower despite gains by golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower despite gains by golds.

* Toronto stocks ended lower on Friday, hurt by a weak Canadian dollar and interest rate jitters. * 78.2 million shares traded worth C$1.04 billion. * Nine of 14 sectors lost ground.
Toronto's key stock index ended lower on Friday, weighed down by a weak Canadian dollar and interest rate jitters.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index shed 29.48 points to close at 5835.31 in moderate turnover of 78.2 million shares worth C$1.04 billion. Declining issues outpaced advances 492 to 405, with 310 issues were flat.

Analysts said a weak dollar and interest rate fears took their toll. "The only thing that really helped us was modest gains in golds, but that just wasn't enough to offset the negatives," said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie.
Twelve of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes ended in negative territory, led by conglomerates, metals and banks.

Conglomerates shed more than 177 points or 2.44 percent to 7092.91, while metals dropped 44.89 points or 0.87 points to 5130.63. The financial services sector fell 46.12 points or 0.77 percent to 5972.17.
The gold group led the gainers, rising 35.82 points or 0.41 percent to 8781.95.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd led actives, closing down 0.35 at 3.25 in heavy trade. The troubled Calgary exploration firm said it expected to receive an interim report by the end of next week on the Busang audit being conducted by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd.

* BC Sugar Refinery Ltd shares ended up 2.35 at 14.96 on turnover of more than 1.2 million shares after Balaclava Enterprises Ltd said it intended to make an offer to buy 7.85 million common shares of the sugar company at C$15 each.
* Placer Dome shares were up 0.30 at 22.25 as more than one million shares traded. The gold miner said on Thursday it would sell its Endako molybdenum mine in British Columbia.
